title: The Genetic Code & Crick's Wobble Hypothesis
topic: Triplet Code, Degeneracy, AUG Start, Stop Codons, & Inosine Wobble
quickSummary: Genetic code: 64 triplet codons (61 sense codons + 3 stop codons: UAA Ochre, UAG Amber, UGA Opal). Properties: degenerate (redundant), unambiguous, non-overlapping, universal. AUG = start + Methionine. Crick's Wobble hypothesis: 5' Inosine on tRNA anticodon pairs with U, C, or A at 3' mRNA codon.

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: The Genetic Code is a triplet code (64 codons: 61 sense + 3 nonsense/stop: UAA, UAG, UGA). Core properties: Degeneracy (20 amino acids coded by 61 codons), Unambiguous (each codon codes for only 1 amino acid), and Universal. AUG is dual-function (start codon + Met). Crick's Wobble Hypothesis allows relaxed non-Watson-Crick base pairing at the 3' base of the mRNA codon.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 7.1 Salient Features of the Genetic Code
1. **Triplet Nature**: $3\text{ consecutive nucleotides}$ in mRNA constitute $1\text{ codon}$ ($4^3 = 64\text{ codons}$). Marshall Nirenberg, Severo Ochoa, and Har Gobind Khorana deciphered the code.
2. **61 Sense Codons & 3 Stop Codons**:
   - **Start Codon**: **AUG** (codes for Methionine in eukaryotes; N-formylmethionine in prokaryotes).
   - **Stop / Nonsense Codons**: **UAA (Ochre), UAG (Amber), and UGA (Opal)**.
3. **Degeneracy (Redundancy)**: Most amino acids are specified by more than one codon (e.g., Leucine, Serine, and Arginine each have $6\text{ codons}$). Tryptophan (UGG) and Methionine (AUG) have only one codon each.
4. **Unambiguous & Non-Overlapping**: A given codon codes for one and only one amino acid, read continuously without punctuation.

### 7.2 Crick’s Wobble Hypothesis (1966)
- Explains how $30\text{--}40\text{ distinct tRNA species}$ can decode all 61 sense codons.

```
                       WOBBLE PAIRING AT 3rd CODON BASE
                       
     5' ─────── mRNA Codon:   G  ─  C  ─  [ U / C / A ] (3rd Base Wobble)
                               │     │        │
     3' ─── tRNA Anticodon:   C  ─  G  ─  [  INOSINE  ] (1st Base Anticodon)
```

- **Mechanics**: Steric constraints are relaxed exclusively at the **$3'$ base of the mRNA codon** and **$5'$ base of the tRNA anticodon**.
  - An **Inosine ($\text{I}$)** residue at the $5'$ position of the anticodon forms flexible hydrogen bonds with **$\text{U}$, $\text{C}$, or $\text{A}$** at the $3'$ position of the codon.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Non-Standard Genetic Code Exceptions
conceptBreakdown.title: Non-Standard Genetic Code Exceptions
conceptBreakdown.content: Minor exceptions exist in mitochondrial genomes and ciliates: in human mitochondria, UGA codes for Tryptophan (instead of stop) and AUA codes for Methionine (instead of Isoleucine).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 21st and 22nd Genetically Encoded Amino Acids
conceptBreakdown.title: 21st and 22nd Genetically Encoded Amino Acids
conceptBreakdown.content: Selenocysteine (21st amino acid) is inserted at specific UGA codons via SECIS RNA stem-loop elements, and Pyrrolysine (22nd amino acid) is inserted at UAG in certain methanogenic archaea.
